ci.yml.legs:
name: legs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      matrix_port: ${{ steps.legs.outputs.matrix_port }}
      matrix_oracle: ${{ steps.legs.outputs.matrix_oracle }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: the planner can say no (ci/legs-test.py)
        run: python3 ci/legs-test.py
      - name: the macOS split preserves every campaign and measurement
        run: python3 -I ci/macos-split-test.py
      - name: the legs
        id: legs
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: python3 ci/legs.py --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
ci.yml.port:
needs: legs
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The legs are the plan's (ci/legs.py): linux x86-64 and aarch64
        # (`builds: false`, where the job asserts both refusals by name)
        # for a pull request and a trunk push; macOS arm64 too every night
        # and on a dispatch (tl30).
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.legs.outputs.matrix_port || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # 180 since yw05: campaign 05's suites grow both unit lanes (the
    # 512-tab cap, the 100,000-op group storm) — at yw05's tabs merge the
    # job took 119 minutes to reach its last fuzzer (run 39818758061).
    # 240 since yw06 for macOS's nightly leg only, which still runs both
    # unit lanes and the fuzzers in this job; on Linux they are the `unit`
    # and `fuzz` jobs below, and this job is the build (~24 minutes in run
    # 40037661631), the tables and the walk's listings.
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.os == 'macos-latest' && 240 || 60 }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      - name: wolf fmt --check
        run: tools/check-fmt

      - name: harness scratch homes (yew#11)
        run: python3 -I tools/check-test-env

      - name: named golden divergence controls
        run: python3 -I tools/goldens-pty-test.py

      - name: build, both tiers
        if: matrix.builds
        run: tools/build --all

      - name: both tiers are refused on this host, by name (wolf-lang#614)
        if: ${{ !matrix.builds }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set +e
          tools/build --native >native.log 2>&1
          n=$?
          tools/build --release >release.log 2>&1
          r=$?
          set -e
          cat native.log release.log
          if [ "$n" = 0 ] || [ "$r" = 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::a tier now builds on linux aarch64 (native $n, release $r); widen the matrix"
            exit 1
          fi
          grep -q "this host cannot run the native tier" native.log
          grep -q "this host cannot run the release tier" release.log

      - name: --version is C yew's two lines
        if: matrix.builds
        shell: bash
        run: |
          target/release/yew --version >version.txt
          printf 'yew 1.0.0-dev\nmodules: lsp ai fuss plugins\n' | cmp - version.txt

      - name: the tables are the generator's, and sagitta's
        if: matrix.builds
        run: tools/check-tables

      - name: wolf test (campaign 00's suites, warnings denied)
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        run: tools/check-test

      - name: the same tests natively
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        run: tools/check-test --native

      # yw06 (R-yw06-10, s26): the walk and .gitignore over the C input
      # witness's two fixture trees (`.git/info/exclude` unread, the
      # `.git/info/.gitignore` C reads, a nested anchor's NULL base), the
      # listings byte for byte pinned C's (tools/walk-listings/c.json).
      - name: the walk's listings are C's (R-yw06-10)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.builds }}
        run: tools/check-walk-listings

      # s02 DoD 8: the decoder and segmenter fuzzer, 200,000 iterations,
      # seed 1, the nine invariants (tools/fuzz-unicode/main.lu).
      - name: fuzz the decoder and the segmenter
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-unicode --iters 200000 --seed 1

      # s12 (yw02): the differential fuzz of the piece tree, undo, marks,
      # cursors, snapshots and save against sagitta's naive oracle under
      # its own generator (tools/fuzz-textbuf/main.lu), the smoke trace
      # replayed first, 200,000 ops at two seeds; exit is the driver's.
      - name: the differential fuzz of the text engine, two seeds
        if: ${{ matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/run-fuzz-textbuf --iters=200000 --seed=1
          target/tools/fuzz-textbuf --iters=200000 --seed=0x243f6a8885a308d3

      # yw04 (s18.5 §1): sagitta's fuzz_fuzzy over ws.fuzzy, the scorer
      # and ranker's properties, 200,000 inputs at two seeds.
      - name: fuzz the fuzzy scorer, two seeds
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/run-fuzz-fuzzy --iters 200000 --seed 1
          tools/run-fuzz-fuzzy --iters 200000 --seed 2

      # yw04 (s20 DoD 6-7, s21 DoD 13): the regex engine's fuzzers at CI
      # size — fuzz_re_diff against the ported re_ref oracle, fuzz_re_compile
      # (err.off in range), fuzz_re_quote; the inputs are C's harness's bit
      # for bit (the report's hash= is C's). The DoD campaign is kasumi's
      # (notes/yw04-evidence/regex/fuzz-campaign.txt).
      - name: fuzz the regex engine (CI size)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-re --ci

      # yw04 (s57.23, s57.25): the shell context lexer's and the --help
      # parser's fuzzers over fuzzlib's generator ported bit for bit
      # (tools/fuzzgen): the report's hash= is C's for the same seed.
      - name: fuzz the shell context lexer and the help parser
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/build-fuzz-shell
          FUZZ_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-fuzz-shctx --iters=200000
          FUZZ_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-fuzz-comphelp

      # yw04 (s21 DoD 13): search, overlay, replace, edit, jump and undo
      # interleaved over fuzzlib's generator (C's run_session), every
      # invariant after every operation, four seeds of 500 sessions
      # (~23,000 operations each, DoD 13's 10,000); the 2,000-session seeds
      # and the 200,000-session campaign are kasumi's
      # (notes/yw04-evidence/search/fuzz-search.txt).
      - name: fuzz search, replace and the jump lists, four seeds
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.builds && runner.os != 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/run-fuzz-search --iters=500 --seed=1
          for s in 2 3 4; do FUZZ_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-fuzz-search --iters=500 --seed=$s; done

      # yw08: the pinned Fletch unit cases (test_fl_*.c), each a
      # registry-named test function called in registry order; 213 through
      # s33, 283 with yw09's s34 files (marshal to hook) and s35's
      # fl_replay_runtime.
      - name: the 283 pinned Fletch cases, by name and in registry order
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          python3 -I tools/check-fl-cases --selftest
          python3 -I tools/check-fl-cases

      # yw09: sagitta's check-cmd-dispatch.sh and check-fl-choke.sh (s34
      # DoD 3 and 5) in the port's terms: one dispatch arm per command, and
      # no Fletch-side file mutates the editor around the invoke. Each
      # refuses its own plants first.
      - name: named-command integrity and the Fletch mutation choke point
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          python3 -I tools/check-cmd-dispatch --selftest
          python3 -I tools/check-cmd-dispatch
          tools/check-fl-choke --selftest
          tools/check-fl-choke

  # yw06: the Linux port job's two unit lanes as three shards side by side.
  # Run 40037661631 cut the one job at its 240-minute cap (wolf test 92
  # minutes, the native lane 120, the fuzzers never reached).
  # `tools/check-test --shard I/N` takes every Nth file of the sorted list,
  # so the three shards are every file once (~70 minutes each from that
  # run's per-file times). macOS's nightly port leg still runs both lanes
  # whole in its own job.
  # yw09: six shards. Campaign 07 put the Fletch bridge inside `edit`, which
  # doubled every editor test file's build (run 40637594043: shard 2/3's
  # wolf test lane 35 -> 68 minutes, its native lane cut at the 120) and
  # added 30 test files; six shards are ~40 minutes a lane from that run.
ci.yml.unit:
needs: legs
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
    name: unit (linux x86-64, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/6)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      - name: wolf test, this shard (warnings denied)
        run: tools/check-test --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/6

      - name: the same tests natively, this shard
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: tools/check-test --native --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/6

  # yw06: the Linux fuzzers as jobs of their own, every CI size unchanged.
  # Run 40037661631 found the port job's fuzzers past its cap and the oracle
  # job cut at its 180 minutes in fuzz_groups. Three families, balanced from
  # that run's step times: the port's own fuzzers (~45 minutes, no C), and
  # the campaigns against C's drivers in two halves (~60 and ~50 minutes,
  # tools/oracle building the drivers first). macOS oracle campaigns run
  # in macos-fuzz; port-only macOS fuzzers remain in the nightly port job.
  # yw09: five families. Campaign 07 doubled each editor-linked release
  # build (run 40637594043: fuzz_tabs 21 -> 42 minutes, 40 of them the
  # build), so port and against-c-2 passed their 120. port-2 takes the
  # search fuzz; against-c-3 takes campaign 07's three, built on the native
  # tier (a minute or two to build, the report lines tier-independent:
  # kasumi's record ran fuzz_record and the round trip native too). Run
  # 40692505908 then read against-c-1 at 109 and against-c-2 at 103 of
  # their 120 minutes and against-c-3 at 17: fuzz_state and fuzz_mouse
  # (from c-1) and fuzz_gitignore and the four fl drivers (from c-2) move
  # to against-c-3, about 70, 86 and 48 minutes from that run's steps.
ci.yml.fuzz:
needs: legs
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        family: [port, port-2, against-c-1, against-c-2, against-c-3]
    name: fuzz (linux x86-64, ${{ matrix.family }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: C yew at the pin, its drivers built
        if: matrix.family != 'port' && matrix.family != 'port-2'
        run: tools/oracle --cc gcc --build-only

      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      # s02 DoD 8: the decoder and segmenter fuzzer, 200,000 iterations,
      # seed 1, the nine invariants (tools/fuzz-unicode/main.lu).
      - name: fuzz the decoder and the segmenter
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'port' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-unicode --iters 200000 --seed 1

      # s12 (yw02): the differential fuzz of the piece tree, undo, marks,
      # cursors, snapshots and save against sagitta's naive oracle under
      # its own generator (tools/fuzz-textbuf/main.lu), the smoke trace
      # replayed first, 200,000 ops at two seeds; exit is the driver's.
      - name: the differential fuzz of the text engine, two seeds
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'port' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/run-fuzz-textbuf --iters=200000 --seed=1
          target/tools/fuzz-textbuf --iters=200000 --seed=0x243f6a8885a308d3

      # yw04 (s18.5 §1): sagitta's fuzz_fuzzy over ws.fuzzy, the scorer
      # and ranker's properties, 200,000 inputs at two seeds.
      - name: fuzz the fuzzy scorer, two seeds
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'port' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/run-fuzz-fuzzy --iters 200000 --seed 1
          tools/run-fuzz-fuzzy --iters 200000 --seed 2

      # yw04 (s20 DoD 6-7, s21 DoD 13): the regex engine's fuzzers at CI
      # size — fuzz_re_diff against the ported re_ref oracle, fuzz_re_compile
      # (err.off in range), fuzz_re_quote; the inputs are C's harness's bit
      # for bit (the report's hash= is C's). The DoD campaign is kasumi's
      # (notes/yw04-evidence/regex/fuzz-campaign.txt).
      - name: fuzz the regex engine (CI size)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'port' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-re --ci

      # yw04 (s57.23, s57.25): the shell context lexer's and the --help
      # parser's fuzzers over fuzzlib's generator ported bit for bit
      # (tools/fuzzgen): the report's hash= is C's for the same seed.
      - name: fuzz the shell context lexer and the help parser
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'port' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/build-fuzz-shell
          FUZZ_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-fuzz-shctx --iters=200000
          FUZZ_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-fuzz-comphelp

      # yw04 (s21 DoD 13): search, overlay, replace, edit, jump and undo
      # interleaved over fuzzlib's generator (C's run_session), every
      # invariant after every operation, four seeds of 500 sessions
      # (~23,000 operations each, DoD 13's 10,000); the 2,000-session seeds
      # and the 200,000-session campaign are kasumi's
      # (notes/yw04-evidence/search/fuzz-search.txt).
      - name: fuzz search, replace and the jump lists, four seeds
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'port-2' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/run-fuzz-search --iters=500 --seed=1
          for s in 2 3 4; do FUZZ_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-fuzz-search --iters=500 --seed=$s; done

      # yw04: Sprint 18's parser fuzz (s18 DoD 10) — the port's driver
      # (tools/fuzz-cmdparse, C's generator bit for bit) and C's own at
      # 1,000,000 inputs, seed 1: zero failures and the two report lines
      # equal byte for byte (the same inputs, both parsers green).
      - name: fuzz_cmdparse, the port against C's driver (1,000,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-1' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-cmdparse --campaign --against-oracle

      # yw05 (s22 DoD 10): the pane fuzz — random split, close, resize,
      # focus and screen-size sequences, the tree's invariants, live focus,
      # layout idempotence and leaf_at after every operation — the port's
      # driver (tools/fuzz-panes over C's generator) and C's own
      # (build/fuzz_panes, tools/oracle builds it) at 10,000 sessions (~900,000
      # operations) a seed, four seeds, the two report lines equal byte for
      # byte.
      - name: fuzz_panes, the port against C's driver (10,000 sessions x 4 seeds)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-1' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-panes --campaign --against-oracle

      # yw06 (s25 §9, DoD 12): the state fuzz — random bytes and
      # structure-breaking mutations of the frozen v1 corpus through the
      # parser and the schema layer on a fresh editor, 25 documents a case
      # — the port's driver (tools/fuzz-state over C's generator and
      # fuzz_state's dictionary) and C's own (build/fuzz_state, tools/oracle
      # builds it) at the CI size, 2,000 cases at each of the four seeds
      # (s25's 100,000 x 4 is the lane's, kasumi: notes/yw06-evidence/), the
      # two report lines equal byte for byte. The driver is the native
      # tier's: the same cases, minutes of the job's budget saved.
      - name: fuzz_state, the port against C's driver (2,000 cases x 4 seeds)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-state --native --campaign --against-oracle --sessions=2000

      # yw06 (s27 Testing Strategy, s57.13's motion mix, s57.15's 1003
      # rule): the router fuzz — mouse reports as a terminal writes them,
      # through the real decoder into the router, 25,000 events a session,
      # no stuck phase, no tab-array mutation without its release, 1003 off
      # whenever no menu is open and no chevron is drawn — the port's driver
      # (tools/fuzz-mouse over C's generator) and C's own (build/fuzz_mouse)
      # at `make fuzz-mouse`'s size: 4 sessions at each of four seeds,
      # 400,000 events, the report lines equal byte for byte.
      - name: fuzz_mouse, the port against C's driver (4 sessions x 4 seeds)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-mouse --native --campaign --against-oracle

      # yw05 (s23 DoD 2): the tab oracle — random open, close, switch and
      # reorder sequences against a naive list of ids, the whole list and
      # the ACTIVE id compared after every operation — the port's driver
      # (tools/fuzz-tabs over C's generator) and C's own (build/fuzz_tabs,
      # tools/oracle builds it) at 10,000 sessions (~1,200,000 operations)
      # a seed, the pinned seed 1 and a random lane (its seed printed), the
      # two report lines equal byte for byte.
      - name: fuzz_tabs, the port against C's driver (10,000 sessions, the pinned seed and a random lane)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-2' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-tabs --campaign --against-oracle

      # yw05 (s24 DoD 3 and 10): the group fuzz — a session is a 400-step
      # membership storm against a naive oracle (every count and order
      # recomputed and compared after each step and each walk step, no
      # empty group surviving any sequence) and a 400-key picker storm (no
      # invented path) — the port's driver (tools/fuzz-groups over C's
      # generator) and C's own (build/fuzz_groups, tools/oracle builds it)
      # at C's own campaign, 250 sessions a seed at four seeds
      # (Makefile:180-195; 100,000 membership steps a seed), the two
      # report lines equal byte for byte.
      - name: fuzz_groups, the port against C's driver (250 sessions x 4 seeds)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-2' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-groups --campaign --against-oracle

      # yw06 (s26 Testing Strategy, §4): the .gitignore matcher fuzz — the
      # input as a pattern, the 35 adversarial shapes, 64 random patterns
      # and a 32-rule set, every answer bounded — the port's driver
      # (tools/fuzz-gitignore over C's generator) and C's own
      # (build/fuzz_gitignore) at `make fuzz`'s size, 200,000 iterations at
      # seed 1, the two report lines equal byte for byte.
      - name: fuzz_gitignore, the port against C's driver (200,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-gitignore --native --campaign --against-oracle

      # yw07b (s29 DoD, Makefile:2266-2267): fuzz_fl_lex, the lexer's forward
      # progress over the generator stream, 200,000 inputs at seed 1, its
      # report line C's driver's byte for byte (tools/run-fuzz-fl-front).
      - name: fuzz_fl_lex, the port against C's driver (200,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-fl-front lex --against-oracle --iters=200000 --seed=1

      # yw07b fmt (s29 DoD 6 with s36's data seam, s31 DoD 3 and 8;
      # Makefile:2267-2268): fuzz_fl_parse whole, its fl_data_read raw and
      # framed subchecks included, and fuzz_fl_std (every str and fmt native,
      # and the input as a fmt.f template), each report line C's byte for byte.
      - name: fuzz_fl_parse with its data mode, the port against C's driver (200,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # fuzz_fl_lex's step built the same driver (target/tools/fl-front).
          if [ -x target/tools/fl-front ]; then export FUZZ_PREBUILT=1; fi
          tools/run-fuzz-fl-front parse --against-oracle --iters=200000 --seed=1

      - name: fuzz_fl_std, the port against C's driver (200,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-fl-std --against-oracle --iters=200000 --seed=1

      # yw08 (s32 §8 and DoD 8, Makefile:2269): fuzz_fl_vm, source through
      # parse, compile and a deny-all VM at C's step limit, the 13 kinds and a
      # clean VM (sp, frames, handlers, open upvalues) after every input,
      # 200,000 inputs at seed 1 under the five-second per-input watchdog;
      # its report line C's driver's byte for byte, and its tally must show
      # the inputs executed (tools/run-fuzz-fl-vm).
      - name: fuzz_fl_vm, source execution against C's driver (200,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-fl-vm --against-oracle --iters=200000 --seed=1

      # yw09 (s34 §8, Makefile:2270): fuzz_flapi, generational handles held,
      # released, crafted and dropped, and ed.run's marshalling against a
      # scratch editor; every refusal `handle` or `type`, every failed run
      # one of the 13 kinds; its report line C's driver's byte for byte and
      # its tally showing the inputs executed (tools/run-fuzz-flapi).
      - name: fuzz_flapi, handles and ed.run against C's driver (200,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        run: tools/run-fuzz-flapi --native --against-oracle --iters=200000 --seed=1

      # yw09 (s35, Makefile:2372 and :2401): fuzz_record, arbitrary recorder
      # events must emit Fletch that parses with no error; the corpus replayed
      # once (`make test-record-corpus`) and 200,000 inputs at seed 1, each
      # report line C's driver's byte for byte (tools/run-fuzz-record).
      - name: fuzz_record, the recorder's emitter against C's driver (corpus and 200,000 inputs)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        run: |
          tools/run-fuzz-record --native --against-oracle --corpus-only
          FUZZ_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-fuzz-record --against-oracle --iters=200000 --seed=1

      # yw09 (s35 DoD 9/10, R-yw09-1 A, Makefile:4028-4041): the round-trip
      # law at C's 2,000 seeds, six fixtures, four fixed fixtures and the 21
      # recorder corpus files, its report line C's runner's byte for byte,
      # and the planted folding fault shrunk to its three-event prefix
      # (tools/run-roundtrip).
      - name: the round-trip law against C's runner (2,000 seeds, corpus, planted fault)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-3' }}
        run: tools/run-roundtrip --native --against-oracle

  # yw06 (G29, deliverable 8): a test file whose whole run is past the
  # checked machine's 20M-step budget falls back to the native tier under
  # `wolf test`, so its cases get no checked verdict there; each file in
  # tools/check-test-cases.txt runs one case at a time instead, the
  # verdict read from conform-run's JSON. A job of its own, beside the
  # unit shards (27 minutes in run 40037661631).
  # yw07b: the Fletch selector files add ~360 runs to the table's ~470 (33
  # minutes alone in run 40177235318), so `tools/check-test-cases --shard
  # I/4` takes every 4th run of the table's run list: each case and each
  # one-past-the-end run in exactly one shard (its selftest checks the
  # partition), a stale allow row reported once, by shard 1.
ci.yml.checked-cases:
needs: legs
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    name: checked-cases (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      - name: the checked-case adapter rejects native and malformed records
        run: python3 -I tools/check-test-cases-selftest

      - name: a named refusal never becomes a passed case (the allowance controls)
        run: python3 -I tools/test-check-test-cases

      - name: performance MISS rows are exact and host-scoped
        run: python3 -I tools/perf-editor-verdict --selftest

      - name: editor ratios require five C-stable trials
        run: python3 -I tools/perf-editor-samples --selftest

      - name: the checked machine, one case at a time (G29), this shard
        run: python3 -I tools/check-test-cases --shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4
ci.yml.oracle:
needs: legs
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The legs are the plan's (ci/legs.py): linux x86-64, macOS arm64
        # (clang alone) and linux aarch64 (C yew alone, `port: false`), on
        # every event. On macOS this job is the pull request's macOS smoke:
        # the port built there and its pty goldens, the terminal (tl30).
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.legs.outputs.matrix_oracle || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Run 40138357879 hit 210m on macOS. Its ~80m build/golden slice
    # stays here; campaigns and measurements have separate capped jobs.
    # yw09: campaign 07 doubled every release build of the editor (run
    # 40692505908: the port 20 -> 41 minutes, demo_paint 16 -> 39,
    # perf_cmdcomp past its 30), so the slice is ~145 minutes on macOS
    # and ~180 on ubuntu with its measurements; the hard compile gates
    # stay here (ci/macos-split-test.py), so the caps move, not the gates.
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.os == 'macos-latest' && 180 || 210 }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: C yew at the pin, built and its unit suite run
        shell: bash
        run: tools/oracle ${{ matrix.ccs }} --unit

      # yw03: the command registry's table is the generator's output
      # over sagitta's cmd.c at the pin, and runtime/ is sagitta's
      # runtime/ byte for byte with the embedded copy regenerated from it.
      - name: the registry table, the runtime copy and the shell corpora are the pin's
        run: |
          tools/check-cmdtab
          tools/check-runtime
          tools/check-shell-fixtures
          tools/check-yw06-cases --selftest
          tools/check-fletch-spec

      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        if: matrix.port
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      - name: build the port, release tier
        if: matrix.port
        run: tools/build --release

      - name: build the port's demo_paint (tools/demo-paint, release tier)
        if: matrix.port
        run: tools/build-demo

      - name: clipboard subprocess regressions with the pinned oracle helper
        if: matrix.port && runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export YEW_ROOT=$PWD
          . tools/lib-toolchain.sh
          mkdir -p target/tests
          "$WOLF" build --deny-warnings src/text_clipboard_test.lu -o target/tests/text_clipboard_test
          docker run --rm --init --pids-limit 4096 --memory 8g --ulimit core=0 \
            -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" \
            -e YEW_ROOT="$PWD" -e YEW_RUNTIME_DIR="$PWD/runtime" ubuntu:24.04 bash -c '
              set -e
              . tools/lib-test-env.sh
              test_env_begin
              target/tests/text_clipboard_test
            ' >target/tests/clipboard.out 2>&1
          cat target/tests/clipboard.out
          grep -q '^clipboard_unread_writer_times_out: PASS' target/tests/clipboard.out
          ! grep -q 'SKIP' target/tests/clipboard.out

      # yw02's torture gate (M-YW2's campaign-02 surface, contract §8):
      # sagitta's own `kill9` driver and fault shim over the PORT's torture
      # child (tools/yew-torture, release tier), no external kills
      # (`YEW_TORTURE_SIGKILL_ITERS=0`), through the unit test that ports
      # `save_fault_shim_contract` — every sweep must hold. Since the 0.2.34
      # pin the save syncs (G3, wolf-lang#796; yw05), so the driver exits 0
      # and G3's KNOWN-RED acceptance is gone. The driver and shim exist
      # where the oracle builds `torture-build` (linux); on macOS the test
      # says SKIP by name.
      - name: build the port's torture child (tools/yew-torture, release tier)
        if: matrix.port
        run: tools/build-torture

      - name: sagitta's kill9 driver over the port's torture child
        if: matrix.port && runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export YEW_ROOT=$PWD
          . tools/lib-toolchain.sh
          mkdir -p target/tests
          "$WOLF" build --deny-warnings src/text_save_paths_test.lu -o target/tests/text_save_paths_test
          target/tests/text_save_paths_test >target/tests/save-paths.out 2>&1 || { cat target/tests/save-paths.out target/tests/save-shim-contract.log; exit 1; }
          cat target/tests/save-paths.out target/tests/save-shim-contract.log
          grep -qx "save_paths_test: 10 cases pass" target/tests/save-paths.out
          ! grep -q "SKIP save_fault_shim_contract" target/tests/save-paths.out

      # macOS: the driver interposes the shim with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES
      # (`kill9.c:204-215`) over a wolf binary, which yw02 could not run
      # (no builds on the lane's Mac, track rule): RECORDED until a lane
      # reads its log and gates it.
      - name: sagitta's kill9 driver over the port's torture child on macOS (recorded)
        if: matrix.port && runner.os == 'macOS'
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: the kill9 driver over the port's torture child is RECORDED on macOS (DYLD interposition over a wolf binary, unmeasured by yw02)"
          export YEW_ROOT=$PWD
          . tools/lib-toolchain.sh
          mkdir -p target/tests
          "$WOLF" build --deny-warnings src/text_save_paths_test.lu -o target/tests/text_save_paths_test
          target/tests/text_save_paths_test

      # kill9.c's late lanes (EINTR, ENOSPC, determinism, the 500 external
      # SIGKILLs) through tools/torture-replica.py, line for line, three
      # ways: the port's child checked by the port, the port's child checked
      # by C (C replays the port's journals) and C's child checked by the
      # port (the port replays C's). Signals only inside a container (RULES
      # §5). Since the 0.2.34 pin the port's save syncs (G3; yw05), so every
      # lane holds every way, the determinism order included.
      - name: kill9's late lanes in a container, the replica three ways (linux)
        if: matrix.port && runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          b=$PWD/target/oracle/sagitta/build
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" ubuntu:24.04 bash -c '
            set -e
            apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && apt-get install -y -qq python3 >/dev/null
            b='"$b"'
            s=$b/tests/torture/faultshim.so
            python3 tools/torture-replica.py --child target/tools/yew-torture --checker "$b/yew-torture" --shim "$s" --lanes eintr,enospc,sigkill >target/tests/replica-port-c.out 2>&1 || true
            python3 tools/torture-replica.py --child "$b/yew-torture" --checker target/tools/yew-torture --shim "$s" >target/tests/replica-c-port.out 2>&1 || true
            python3 tools/torture-replica.py --child target/tools/yew-torture --checker target/tools/yew-torture --shim "$s" >target/tests/replica-port-port.out 2>&1 || true
          '
          cat target/tests/replica-port-c.out target/tests/replica-c-port.out target/tests/replica-port-port.out
          grep -q "^replica: GREEN$" target/tests/replica-port-c.out
          grep -q "^replica: GREEN$" target/tests/replica-c-port.out
          grep -q "^replica: GREEN$" target/tests/replica-port-port.out

      # yw04 (deliverable 6, R-yw02-1 = A): the live-editor torture lane —
      # sagitta's kill9 driver and fault shim over the port's EDITOR (its
      # yew-live-torture types Ndd, a bracketed paste, s and
      # :ed.quit_force, arming the shim with SIGUSR2), then the port's
      # replica for the 500 external SIGKILLs and the determinism lane over
      # kill9's one shared state home (since yw06 the `:` history is per
      # workspace, s25 §8, so the shared run must reproduce: the KNOWN-RED
      # and its per-run acceptance are gone). Since the 0.2.34 pin the save
      # syncs (G3; yw05): tools/torture-live exits 0 only when every lane
      # holds; signals inside a container (RULES §5).
      - name: the live-editor torture lane in a container (linux)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os == 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" ubuntu:24.04 bash -c '
            set -e
            apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && apt-get install -y -qq python3 >/dev/null
            tools/torture-live --yew target/release/yew
          '

      # yw04 (s20 §Testing): the 188 golden rows the port's test_re_match
      # replays are sagitta's re_golden.h at the pin, row for row.
      - name: the regex golden table is the pin's
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        run: tools/check-re-golden

      # yw04 (s18.5 §4): the per-keystroke completion gate, the port's
      # harness beside sagitta's perf_cmdcomp from the same run. An
      # ANNOUNCED ADVISORY on the hosted runner; kasumi under taskset -c
      # 0-3 is the record (notes/yw04-execute-and-search.md §4).
      # yew#44: compile errors are fatal, timing remains advisory. This is
      # in the oracle job, not the already-long ubuntu port job. Build once.
      # 30 since yw06: the harness stages util through edit and builds them
      # on the release tier, and campaign 05's second half put that past
      # 15 minutes on the hosted runner (PR #50's run 40011667289: the step
      # cut off at 15m13s; 12.5 minutes on kasumi's shared cores).
      # 60 since yw09: campaign 07 put the Fletch bridge in `edit`, and run
      # 40692505908 cut the step at its 30 on both hosts (the port's own
      # release build there took 41 minutes on ubuntu, 36 on macOS).
      - name: build perf_cmdcomp harnesses (hard gate)
        if: matrix.port
        timeout-minutes: 60
        run: |
          python3 -I tools/check-perf-cmdcomp-build
          tools/run-perf-cmdcomp --build-only

      - name: the 2× gate, perf_cmdcomp against C's (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS'
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 15
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: perf_cmdcomp's 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw04-execute-and-search.md §4)"
          PERF_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-perf-cmdcomp --trials 100

      # yw04 (s20 DoD 2-3): the regex gates — the pathological table and
      # the throughput rows, C's in-process harnesses beside the port's
      # from the same run. An ANNOUNCED ADVISORY here, as perf_cmdcomp's.
      - name: the 2× gate, the regex engine against C's (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS'
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 20
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: the regex engine's 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw04-execute-and-search.md §4)"
          tools/run-perf-re --bytes 268435456

      # yw01's gate (contract §7, ruling #89 R3): the campaign-01 PTY
      # cases against the port's demo_paint, each by name so a missing
      # case is a red row, not a silent skip; `version` and `help`
      # against the port's own binary, byte for byte. osc52_frame, the
      # clipboard's case (sprint 12), is gated here since yw02 ported
      # `text.clipboard` and the demo's osc52 scene; osc52_reply holds
      # from yw01.
      - name: goldens, campaign 01 (yw01's gate; osc52_frame from yw02)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --suite version,help
          cases="probe_modern probe_dumb paint_basic paint_wide paint_colors_truecolor paint_colors_256 paint_colors_16 paint_damage paint_resize restore_quit restore_crash restore_bus restore_abrt restore_suspend input_keys_modern input_keys_legacy osc52_reply osc52_frame"
          # macOS: restore_bus runs in the advisory step below (R-yw01-1: the
          # guard's post-mortem restore races the harness's reap-time check
          # there, run 39350728011). restore_abrt is gated on every host since
          # yw05: the port listens for ABORT and restores in process before
          # the death, as C's handler does (tty.c:381-384).
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = macOS ]; then
            cases=$(echo "$cases" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -vx -e restore_bus | tr '\n' ' ')
          fi
          for c in $cases; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --demo target/tools/demo_paint --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -q "^pty: $c: ok\$" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
          done

      # A SIGBUS the harness SENDS runs no code of the process: the stack
      # guard owns SIGBUS and SIGSEGV (send-only, no program listens), and
      # the runtime's restore at exit (os_term_restore_at_exit, wolf-lang#794,
      # since the 0.2.34 pin) covers only the exits the runtime owns —
      # measured: notes/yw05-evidence/wait/witness/restore-at-exit/. So the
      # guard process (#93 R1 B) still restores AFTER the death, and
      # sagitta's harness checks the restore once, at the reap. Linux wins
      # that race (gated above); macOS lost it for `restore_bus` (run
      # 39350728011). Recorded here, not gated (R-yw01-1).
      - name: goldens, the outside-SIGBUS restore case on macOS (advisory, R-yw01-1)
        if: matrix.port && runner.os == 'macOS'
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: restore_bus is RECORDED on macOS (an outside SIGBUS runs no code of the process, so the guard restores after the death and races the harness's reap-time check; R-yw01-1)"
          for c in restore_bus; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --demo target/tools/demo_paint --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -q "^pty: $c: ok\$" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
          done

      # yw03's gate (M-YW3, contract §6): the campaign-03 PTY goldens,
      # each by name against the release editor (and, for the twelve s15
      # demo scenes, the port's demo_paint), so a missing case is a red
      # row: the notepad (s14), the view (s15), the W and B engines (s16)
      # and H with the cursor sets (s17).
      - name: goldens, campaign 03 (yw03's gate, M-YW3)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cases="notepad_open notepad_move notepad_insert notepad_escape notepad_save notepad_save_error notepad_dirty_write notepad_dirty_discard notepad_dirty_cancel notepad_recover_apply notepad_recover_discard notepad_recover_escape notepad_preserve_lf notepad_preserve_crlf notepad_preserve_bom notepad_preserve_no_final_nl notepad_preserve_invalid notepad_preserve_unicode notepad_burst_keys notepad_burst_paste notepad_restore_term notepad_restore_segv notepad_restore_suspend notepad_restore_kill notepad_quit_force"
          cases="$cases s15_degenerate s15_gutter_abs_1 s15_gutter_hybrid_10 s15_gutter_hybrid_100 s15_gutter_rel_9 s15_metadata_binary_invalid s15_metadata_bom s15_metadata_crlf s15_metadata_mixed s15_mode_i s15_mode_l s15_nowrap_cjk s15_position_unicode s15_resize_roundtrip s15_wrap_cjk"
          cases="$cases s16_block_c_expand s16_block_prose_expand s16_word_emoji s16_word_han_first s16_word_han_second s16_word_tail"
          cases="$cases s17_char_delete_matches_highlight s17_char_selection_unicode_tab s17_h_b_extends_by_block s17_h_c_extends_by_character s17_h_l_extends_by_line s17_h_w_extends_by_word s17_h_w_keyboard_entry s17_lift_ends_draws_two_cursors s17_lift_lines_draws_seven_cursors s17_lift_lines_draws_thousand_cursors s17_line_selection_unicode_tab s17_modal_milestone_saves s17_multicursor_typing_is_simultaneous s17_one_undo_reverts_multicursor_typing s17_rect_selection_unicode_tab s17_secondary_cursors_draw_at_eol"
          # macOS: the two outside-signal restore cases (SIGSEGV and SIGKILL
          # from the harness: no code of the process runs, so the guard
          # restores after the death, G1) run in the advisory step below, as
          # campaign 01's restore_bus does (R-yw01-1; run 39490908160 lost
          # notepad_restore_segv's reap-time check there).
          # The two burst cases are gated on macOS again since yw05 (yew#28):
          # sagitta's harness writes a 4 KiB burst without reading the
          # child's output (`write_master`, `tests/pty/harness.c:267-298`),
          # and at wolf 0.2.33 the port's wait switched termios modes (the
          # VTIME tick, the drain, the fine wait), each a
          # tcsetattr(TCSADRAIN) that could wait on output nobody read
          # (runs 39674542106, 39688445786). Since the 0.2.34 pin the wait is
          # one os_signal_wait_fds and the raw mode is set once.
          want=62
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = macOS ]; then
            cases=$(echo "$cases" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -vx -e notepad_restore_segv -e notepad_restore_kill | tr '\n' ' ')
            want=60
          fi
          n=0
          for c in $cases; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --demo target/tools/demo_paint --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -q "^pty: $c: ok\$" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
            n=$((n + 1))
          done
          echo "campaign 03: $n goldens green by name"
          [ "$n" = "$want" ]

      - name: goldens, campaign 03's outside-signal restore cases on macOS (advisory, R-yw01-1)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os == 'macOS' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: notepad_restore_segv and notepad_restore_kill are RECORDED on macOS (an outside SIGSEGV or SIGKILL runs no code of the process, so the guard restores after the death and races the harness's reap-time check, as restore_bus; R-yw01-1)"
          for c in notepad_restore_segv notepad_restore_kill; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --demo target/tools/demo_paint --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -q "^pty: $c: ok\$" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
          done

      # yw04's gate (M-YW4): campaign 04's PTY goldens against the release
      # editor, each BY NAME so a missing case is a red row — the prompt
      # (s18, s18.5, s57.17, s57.21, s57.28-s57.31), the shell completion
      # (s57.18, s57.23, s57.24, s57.26, s57.32), and search, replace and
      # the jump lists (s21). Since yw05's 0.2.34 pin all 104: the job half
      # (the stream, the footers, the badge, the region filter both ways,
      # `:r !`, the `*jobs*` table, the generator, `--help` and fish jobs
      # and the persistent session: s19, s57.24-s57.27) over
      # os_signal_wait_fds (G2), and the clipboard writer over os_fork (G30).
      - name: goldens, campaign 04 (yw04's gate, M-YW4)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cases="s18_5_cmdline_click_row s18_5_cmdline_fuzzy_highlight s18_5_cmdline_ghost s18_5_cmdline_ghost_accept s18_5_cmdline_hint s18_5_cmdline_menu_scrolled s18_cmdline_cancel"
          cases="$cases s18_cmdline_completion_escape_restores s18_cmdline_completion_menu s18_cmdline_completion_next s18_cmdline_completion_next_again s18_cmdline_completion_one"
          cases="$cases s18_cmdline_completion_prev_wraps s18_cmdline_completion_printable_closes s18_cmdline_completion_zero s18_cmdline_error_caret s18_cmdline_horizontal_scroll"
          cases="$cases s18_cmdline_menu_enter_not_execute s18_cmdline_open s18_cmdline_selection_seed s18_cmdline_zwj_left s18_cmdline_zwj_right s19_term_is_not_a_feature s21_global_is_a_non_goal"
          cases="$cases s21_named_mark_round_trip s21_overlay_damage_is_narrow s21_replace_all s21_replace_confirm_answers s21_replace_confirm_prompt s21_search_bad_pattern_keeps_screen"
          cases="$cases s21_search_cancel_restores_grid s21_search_count_badge s21_search_direction_after_backward s21_search_highlight_wide s21_search_preview s21_search_word_under_cursor"
          cases="$cases s21_search_wrap_message s21_zero_width_global_terminates s21_zero_width_prefix_final_newline s21_zero_width_prefix_no_final_newline s57_17_fuzzy_one_executes"
          cases="$cases s57_17_pager_arrow_up s57_17_pager_tail_row s57_18_bang_completes_exec s57_18_bang_completes_path s57_18_bang_quotes_a_spacey_path s57_21_insert_home_toggle"
          cases="$cases s57_21_insert_nav_keys s57_21_insert_readline_words s57_21_insert_unix_line_keys s57_23_bang_cd_dirs_only s57_23_bang_dot_slash_exec s57_23_bang_pipe_command_position"
          cases="$cases s57_23_bang_quote_dollar_file s57_23_bang_sudo_wrapper s57_23_bang_variable s57_24_git_remote_add s57_24_make_targets s57_24_ssh_hosts s57_24_wolf_emit_values"
          cases="$cases s57_24_wolf_subcommand s57_26_history_accept_word s57_26_history_ghost s57_26_history_isolated s57_28_prompt_alt_arrow_contextual s57_28_prompt_kill_and_yank"
          cases="$cases s57_28_prompt_last_arg s57_28_prompt_yank_pop s57_29_prompt_select_and_copy s57_29_prompt_select_ascii s57_29_prompt_select_colors_16 s57_29_prompt_select_nocolor s57_29_prompt_select_scrolled"
          cases="$cases s57_29_prompt_type_over s57_30_ctrl_r_search s57_30_substring_history_highlight s57_30_table_bottom_exit s57_30_table_top_to_history s57_30_up_is_history_with_menu_open"
          cases="$cases s57_31_edit_in_buffer_open s57_31_edit_in_buffer_roundtrip s57_31_toggle_sudo s57_32_cd_then_complete s57_32_cd_unknown"
          cases="$cases s19_badge_while_running s19_exit_footer_nonzero s19_exit_footer_ok s19_exit_footer_signal s19_filter_nonzero_keeps_buffer s19_filter_replaces_region"
          cases="$cases s19_filter_typeahead_replays_after_completion s19_jobs_table s19_no_output_message s19_read_at_cursor s19_stream_output s57_24_generator_pending"
          cases="$cases s57_25_help_negative s57_25_help_pending s57_25_help_subcommands s57_26_fish_stub_rows s57_27_completion_follows_session s57_27_session_busy_alongside"
          cases="$cases s57_27_session_cd_persists s57_27_session_exit_recovers"
          n=0
          for c in $cases; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --demo target/tools/demo_paint --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -q "^pty: $c: ok\$" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
            n=$((n + 1))
          done
          echo "campaign 04: $n goldens green by name"
          [ "$n" = 104 ]

      # yw05's gate (contract deliverables 2-5, M-YW5's first half): campaign
      # 05's PTY goldens against the release editor, each BY NAME so a
      # missing case is a red row — Sprint 22's panes (split, nest, focus,
      # resize by key and by drag, close, the refusal, borders beside wide
      # glyphs, click-to-focus on the grapheme) — then Sprint 23's tabs
      # (three tabs, the overflow chevrons, a click on CJK labels, the `*`
      # following undo, the dirty-close question and its discard) and
      # s57.8's ` + ` control clicked — and Sprint 24's groups (the two-row
      # bar, the picker, the negative-payload click, the same-frame jump);
      # startup_multiple_files stays RECORDED below (its snapshot is the
      # :buffers picker, Sprint 26's, yw06).
      - name: goldens, campaign 05 (yw05's gate)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cases="s22_border_beside_wide_glyphs s22_click_focuses_and_lands_on_grapheme s22_click_in_the_right_pane s22_close_restores_full_width s22_drag_border"
          cases="$cases s22_focus_moves_the_accent s22_keyboard_resize s22_nested_three_panes s22_split_h s22_split_refused_when_too_narrow s22_split_v"
          cases="$cases s23_click_switches_with_cjk_labels s23_dirty_close_discard s23_dirty_close_prompt s23_modified_marker_follows_undo s23_overflow_indicators s23_three_tabs"
          cases="$cases s57_8_click_new_tab"
          # Sprint 24's tab groups: the two-row bar, the picker's chrome,
          # the click on a group entry (its negative payload), the jump in
          # the same frame.
          cases="$cases s24_click_enters_a_group s24_digit_jump_is_immediate s24_group_two_row_bar s24_picker_chrome"
          want=22
          n=0
          for c in $cases; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --demo target/tools/demo_paint --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -q "^pty: $c: ok\$" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
            n=$((n + 1))
          done
          echo "campaign 05: $n goldens green by name"
          [ "$n" = "$want" ]

      # yw06's gate (M-YW5 as R-yw06-3 = A shapes it; R-yw06-7 = A): the
      # 81 reachable goldens of deliverables 2-6 by name against the release
      # editor — Sprint 25's resume (2), Sprint 26's finder and pickers (5),
      # the explicit-workspace start and startup_multiple_files (its
      # snapshot the :buffers picker, R-yw05-5), the router's 68 (s27,
      # chrome_ 48, s57.13 less its two FUSS menus, s57.14/15, s57.22;
      # R-yw06-2 = A, one set) and the field repairs (s57.11, s57.12 3).
      # The list is tools/goldens-yw06-cases.txt, held to the pinned C
      # registry in both directions and its order by tools/check-yw06-cases
      # (its selftest plants a missing, a duplicate, a foreign and a
      # reordered list); every name is run, so a missing case is a red row.
      - name: goldens, campaign 05's workspace, finder and mouse (yw06's gate, M-YW5)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 -I tools/check-yw06-cases --selftest
          want=81
          n=0
          for c in $(cat tools/goldens-yw06-cases.txt); do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -q "^pty: $c: ok\$" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
            n=$((n + 1))
          done
          echo "campaign 05 (yw06): $n goldens green by name"
          [ "$n" = "$want" ]

      # yw07b: campaign 06's Fletch core (the adopted contract's deliverables
      # 3, 4, 7 and 8). C yew's own conformance runner over the 39 units of
      # tools/fletch-units.txt, green BY NAME, again under YEW_FL_GC_STRESS=1
      # and a second time byte-compared (sagitta Makefile:4010-4026); the
      # front end's and the compiler's dumps of the 56 corpus files and the
      # three fuzz corpora against C's through `yew fl` (R-yw07-7); and
      # smoke.sh's ten `yew fl` exit-code rows against both binaries.
      - name: goldens, campaign 06's Fletch conformance by name, stressed and twice (yw07b's gate)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/check-fletch-goldens target/release/yew

      # yw08 (s33 §3/§4, deliverable 5; with the step above, M-YW6's fourth
      # artifact): sagitta's own scripts/check-fletch-coverage.sh from the
      # pinned tree with YEW pointed at the port: checks 1-6 (every section,
      # production, native of the port's `yew fl --list-natives`, kind and
      # opcode covered) and check 7 (the ledger byte-identical to the pinned
      # tests/fletch/ledger.txt), the ledger twice byte-compared
      # (Makefile:4021-4025) and --list-natives against C's; first, a dropped
      # and an invented native must each turn the gate red.
      - name: the Fletch coverage gate and its ledger, against the port (yw08)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/check-fletch-coverage target/release/yew

      - name: goldens, the Fletch REPL and hello world, by name (yw08)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          for c in s32_repl_session s33_hello_world_repl s32_bug_restores_the_terminal; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -qx "pty: $c: ok" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
          done

      # yw09's gate (M-YW7): campaign 07's PTY goldens by name against the
      # release editor — s35's three recorder messages, s37's batch that
      # never touches the terminal, s38's six macro-UX cases — and the 69
      # scripts R-yw09-5 A owns (00-47 and the 21 macroux_*) through C's
      # script runner, each BY NAME (`PASS <name>`), the other 25 excluded
      # with their later owners (tools/scripts-deferred.txt) and the two
      # lists held to the pin's 94 by tools/check-yw09-scripts.
      - name: goldens, campaign 07's recorder, batch and macro UX (yw09's gate, M-YW7)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cases="s35_macro_record_start_message s35_macro_record_stop_message s35_macro_record_replay_from_e_mode"
          cases="$cases s37_batch_never_touches_the_terminal"
          cases="$cases s38_macro_indicator_80 s38_macro_indicator_40 s38_macro_edit_flow s38_macro_browser"
          cases="$cases s38_macro_browser_actions s38_macro_indicator_burst"
          n=0
          for c in $cases; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --suite pty --case "$c"
            grep -qx "pty: $c: ok" target/oracle/goldens/pty.log
            n=$((n + 1))
          done
          echo "campaign 07: $n PTY goldens green by name"
          [ "$n" = 10 ]
          python3 -I tools/check-yw09-scripts --selftest
          deferred=$(grep -v '^#' tools/scripts-deferred.txt | cut -f1 | paste -sd, -)
          tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --suite script --script-exclude "$deferred"
          n=0
          for c in $(grep -v '^#' tools/scripts-yw09.txt); do
            # 39_skip_protocol is C's own SKIP (the t.skip protocol).
            verdict=PASS
            [ "$c" = 39_skip_protocol ] && verdict=SKIP
            grep -qE "^$verdict $c( |\$)" target/oracle/goldens/script.log
            n=$((n + 1))
          done
          grep -qE '^script: 69 tests' target/oracle/goldens/script.log
          echo "campaign 07: $n scripts green by name"
          [ "$n" = 69 ]
          # test-script-determinism (Makefile:3930-3947): the runner's
          # --selftest against the port, then a second run of the same 69
          # whose report is byte-identical to the first.
          yew_bin=$(pwd)/target/release/yew
          (cd target/oracle/sagitta && LC_ALL=C build/script_runner --selftest --yew "$yew_bin")
          cp target/oracle/goldens/script.log target/campaign07-script-run-1.log
          tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --suite script --script-exclude "$deferred"
          diff -u target/campaign07-script-run-1.log target/oracle/goldens/script.log
          echo "campaign 07: the script suite's report is deterministic"

      - name: the Fletch invariant report uses its reserved buffer (yw08)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        run: tools/check-fl-report

      - name: the thirteen actual Fletch invariant guards (yw08)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        run: tools/check-fl-invariants

      - name: the Fletch dump differentials, --dump-ast and --dump-bytecode against C
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/check-fl-dump target/release/yew

      # sagitta Makefile:3136-3167: fl_smoke --trace's 21 fixtures, C's
      # CFLAGS_FL_TRACE=1 build in a separate BUILD directory against the
      # port's trace driver, byte for byte after the `# dispatch:` line and
      # twice across processes (R-yw07-3 A: the parity gate re-aimed).
      - name: the Fletch executed-opcode traces against C's, twice
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/check-fl-trace

      - name: yew fl's fourteen smoke rows, C yew and the port (smoke.sh:428-550)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/smoke-fl target/oracle/sagitta/build/yew
          tools/smoke-fl target/release/yew

      # yw06: the in-process state gates' harnesses must COMPILE (yew#44's
      # shape: a compile error is never an advisory timing result); the
      # ratios beside C's own perf_state are the lane's, on kasumi.
      - name: build the perf_state harnesses, C's and the port's (hard gate)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-perf-state --build-only --native

      # yw06 (s27 DoD 13, s57.13 §3, s57.15 §2): the router's harness
      # beside C's perf_mouse must COMPILE (yew#44's shape); the burst, the
      # menu hover and the chevron hover against C's are the lane's, on
      # kasumi (notes/yw06-workspace-finder-mouse.md §4.5).
      - name: build the perf_mouse harnesses, C's and the port's (hard gate)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-perf-mouse --build-only --native

      # yw06 (s26 DoD 6): the finder's harness beside C's perf_finder must
      # COMPILE (yew#44's shape); its four gates against C's are the lane's,
      # on kasumi (notes/yw06-workspace-finder-mouse.md §4.4).
      - name: build the perf_finder harnesses, C's and the port's (hard gate)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-perf-finder --build-only --native

      # yw06 (s25 DoD, test_ws_save.c:961-1189): the two fault-shim rows
      # the port job skips loudly (no oracle there) — the atomic write's
      # order (write, fsync-file, rename, fsync-dir) and kill -9 at each of
      # the 24 fault points — over the pinned shim, natively, in a
      # container (RULES §5: the rows SIGKILL their own children).
      - name: the workspace save's fault-shim rows in a container (linux)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os == 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export YEW_ROOT=$PWD
          . tools/lib-toolchain.sh
          mkdir -p target/tests
          "$WOLF" build --deny-warnings src/edit_ws_save_test.lu -o target/tests/edit_ws_save_test
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" ubuntu:24.04 bash -c '
            set -e
            apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && apt-get install -y -qq python3 >/dev/null
            for i in 25 26; do YEW_LOG=/dev/null YEW_STATE_CASE=$i target/tests/edit_ws_save_test; done
          ' > target/tests/ws-save-shim.out
          cat target/tests/ws-save-shim.out
          grep -q "^ws_save_write_is_atomic_in_order: PASS$" target/tests/ws-save-shim.out
          grep -q "^ws_save_survives_kill9_at_every_step: PASS$" target/tests/ws-save-shim.out

      # yw06 (M-YW5 = R-yw06-3 A): the automated twins of s42 §10's field
      # boxes the port can answer now, over sagitta's own PTY harness
      # (tools/trials/trials.c, its s25 helpers): twenty quit/reopen
      # cycles grid for grid, the restore after SIGKILL, SIGSEGV and a
      # closed terminal, and the C<->port state differential both ways
      # (each editor resumes the other's save; the first saves equal).
      # The runner is built here and run in a container (RULES §5).
      - name: M-YW5's trials, resume and restore, C and the port both ways (linux)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os == 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          tools/run-trials --build-only
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:$PWD" -w "$PWD" ubuntu:24.04 \
            tools/run-trials --prebuilt target/release/yew

      # The rows a later lane ports: red by design, recorded, not gated.
      # The step runs under `continue-on-error` and announces it as a
      # warning annotation on the job, which is what wolf/tools/lane-
      # audit.sh reads as an ANNOUNCED ADVISORY.
      - name: goldens against the port's editor, campaign 05's rows other lanes own (recorded)
        if: matrix.port
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: eleven campaign-05 goldens are RECORDED here, red by design, by owner: s57_9_block_days_structure and _left_eof carry wolf.fl's highlighting in their style rows (yw10); s57_13_fuss_file_menu, _fuss_dir_menu, startup_directory_workspace and the six fuss_drawer_ cases are FUSS's drawer (s56.5 §2-§4, yw13)"
          for c in s57_9_block_days_structure s57_9_block_days_left_eof s57_13_fuss_file_menu s57_13_fuss_dir_menu startup_directory_workspace fuss_drawer_startup_dot fuss_drawer_startup_directory fuss_drawer_enter_tab fuss_drawer_split_h fuss_drawer_split_v fuss_drawer_escape_exact; do
            tools/goldens --yew target/release/yew --suite pty --case "$c" || true
          done

      - name: runtime_locked_mode answers motion, Insert, save and quit
        if: matrix.port
        run: python3 -I notes/yw09b-evidence/runtime-pty.py --yew target/release/yew --runtime runtime --root "${{ runner.temp }}/yw09b-explicit"

      - name: runtime_prefix_skew rejects a foreign install and warns once (linux)
        if: ${{ matrix.port && runner.os == 'Linux' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          fixture="$PWD/target/yw09b-prefix-fixture"
          python3 -I notes/yw09b-evidence/runtime-pty.py --yew target/release/yew --runtime runtime --root "$fixture" --fixture-only
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:$PWD" -v "$fixture/runtime:/usr/local/share/yew/runtime:ro" -w "$PWD" ubuntu:24.04 bash -c '
            set -e
            apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && apt-get install -y -qq python3 >/dev/null
            python3 -I notes/yw09b-evidence/runtime-pty.py --yew target/release/yew --runtime runtime --root "$PWD/target/yw09b-prefix-pty" --prefix
          '

      - name: the harness sees a difference (green on the oracle, red on two plants)
        run: tools/goldens-selftest

      # The 2× gate (contract §7): cold start → first paint and keypress →
      # paint, the port's demo beside C yew's from the same run. The
      # hosted runner is neither quiet nor pinned, so this is an
      # ANNOUNCED ADVISORY here (as sagitta's `enforcement=budget` rows
      # are) until a designated runner exists; the record of truth is
      # kasumi under `taskset -c 0-3` (notes/yw01-the-terminal.md §4).
      - name: the 2× gate, demo_paint against C yew's (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS'
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 10
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: the 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw01-the-terminal.md §4)"
          tools/run-perf-latency --starts 10 --keys 100

      # The 2× gate on the editor (yw03 contract §6): sagitta's own
      # perf_startup and perf_latency harnesses over C yew and the port
      # from the same run, the port/C ratio per row. An ANNOUNCED
      # ADVISORY on the hosted runner, as the demo's; kasumi under
      # `taskset -c 0-3` in a container is the record
      # (notes/yw03-the-modal-core.md §4).
      - name: the 2× gate, the editor against C yew (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS'
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 15
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: the editor's 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw03-the-modal-core.md §4)"
          tools/run-perf-editor

      # yw05: campaign 05's 2× gates (two panes, fifty buffers, the tab
      # switch: tools/run-perf-panes-tabs over sagitta's perf_latency_s56)
      # and the job stream's (tools/run-perf-jobstream over its
      # perf_jobstream), each C, the port, then C again.
      - name: the 2× gate, panes, many buffers and the tab switch against C yew (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 15
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: campaign 05's 2× gates run as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw05-panes-tabs-groups.md §4)"
          tools/run-perf-panes-tabs

      - name: the 2× gate, the job stream against C yew (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 10
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: the job stream's 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw05-panes-tabs-groups.md §4)"
          tools/run-perf-jobstream

      # yw08 (s33 §5, deliverable 6): perf_fletch's thirteen rows, the port's
      # in-process harness beside C's pinned perf_fletch from the same run
      # (tools/run-perf-fletch over tools/fl-headless). Sagitta's own policy
      # for a shared runner (perf_fletch.c:20-30, perf_policy.h): timings
      # are ADVISORY here, so the 2x ratio, the absolute budgets and the
      # two-condition regression gate against tools/perf-fletch-baseline.txt
      # print WARN/MISS without failing, while a zero, a value past 100x a
      # budget, a wrong result or a malformed sample stays a hard failure,
      # as does the gate rules' own selftest. kasumi under taskset in a
      # container is the record (notes/yw08-repl-errors-conformance-perf.md).
      - name: the Fletch bench rows against C's perf_fletch (timing advisory, sanity hard)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS' }}
        timeout-minutes: 20
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-perf-fletch --release --advisory --rows smoke,headless

      # yw09 (R-yw09-3 A): perf_fletch's six editor rows (perf_fletch.c:
      # 1076-1131) under the same gate and the same advisory policy, through
      # tools/fl-editor-perf; insert_100k is C's report-only row. On the
      # NATIVE tier here: a release build of the whole editor is ~40 minutes
      # on this runner (run 40637594043 cut the job in it), the timings are
      # advisory either way, and the sanity bounds, results and samples stay
      # hard. The release record is kasumi's (tools/perf-fletch-baseline.txt).
      - name: the Fletch editor rows against C's perf_fletch (native tier, timing advisory, sanity hard)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.port && runner.os != 'macOS' }}
        timeout-minutes: 30
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-perf-fletch --native --advisory --rows editor

      # Archive, rather than upload individual executables: tar preserves
      # execute bits and the oracle's build -> build-clang symlink.
      - name: Package this head's macOS measurement inputs
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && matrix.port
        run: |
          git rev-parse HEAD > target/macos-oracle-head
          tar -czf target/macos-oracle.tar.gz target/macos-oracle-head \
            target/oracle/sagitta target/release/yew target/tools/demo_paint \
            target/perf-cmdcomp/perf-cmdcomp
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && matrix.port
        with:
          name: macos-oracle
          path: target/macos-oracle.tar.gz
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3
          overwrite: true

  # Seven unchanged macOS oracle campaigns, balanced from run 40138357879:
  # cmdparse/panes/state/mouse ~59m; tabs/groups/gitignore ~50m, plus C build.
  # Two jobs, not one per fuzzer; the nightly's port-only fuzzers stay put.
ci.yml.macos-fuzz:
needs: legs
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        family: [against-c-1, against-c-2]
    name: fuzz (macOS arm64, ${{ matrix.family }})

        run: tools/run-fuzz-cmdparse --campaign --against-oracle

        run: tools/run-fuzz-mouse --native --campaign --against-oracle

        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-2' }}

      - name: fuzz_panes, the port against C's driver (10,000 sessions x 4 seeds)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-1' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-panes --campaign --against-oracle


      - name: fuzz_tabs, the port against C's driver (10,000 sessions, the pinned seed and a random lane)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-2' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-tabs --campaign --against-oracle


      - name: fuzz_groups, the port against C's driver (250 sessions x 4 seeds)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'against-c-2' }}
        shell: bash
        run: tools/run-fuzz-groups --campaign --against-oracle


  # Four added jobs total: two fuzz families above, two measurement families
  # here. Existing hard compile gates stay in oracle; it hands off only
  # this run/head's inputs (never a cross-run cache). Advisory policy is unchanged.
ci.yml.macos-perf:
needs: [legs, oracle]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        family: [editor, components]
    name: perf (macOS arm64, ${{ matrix.family }})
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: macos-oracle
          path: target/macos-input
      - name: Restore and verify this head's macOS measurement inputs
        run: |
          tar -xzf target/macos-input/macos-oracle.tar.gz
          test "$(cat target/macos-oracle-head)" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          test -x target/release/yew
          test -x target/tools/demo_paint
          test -x target/perf-cmdcomp/perf-cmdcomp
          test -x target/oracle/sagitta/build/yew
      - name: the pinned toolchain, by digest
        run: tools/fetch-toolchain

      - name: the 2× gate, perf_cmdcomp against C's (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'components' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 15
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: perf_cmdcomp's 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw04-execute-and-search.md §4)"
          PERF_PREBUILT=1 tools/run-perf-cmdcomp --trials 100


      - name: the 2× gate, the regex engine against C's (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'components' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 20
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: the regex engine's 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw04-execute-and-search.md §4)"
          tools/run-perf-re --bytes 268435456


      - name: the 2× gate, demo_paint against C yew's (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'components' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 10
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::continue-on-error: the 2× gate runs as an ADVISORY on the hosted runner (unpinned, not quiet); kasumi under taskset -c 0-3 is the record (notes/yw01-the-terminal.md §4)"
          tools/run-perf-latency --starts 10 --keys 100


      - name: the 2× gate, the editor against C yew (advisory on the hosted runner)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.family == 'editor' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 60
        shell: bash
        run: |

name: nightly red, an issue
    needs: [legs, port, unit, fuzz, checked-cases, oracle, macos-fuzz, macos-perf]
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:

      - name: open or update the nightly-red issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: ci/nightly-red.sh

float-hosts.yml.oracle:
strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-14]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Record public C conversion answers
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          export YEW_ROOT="$PWD" YEW_RUNTIME_DIR="$PWD/runtime"
          . tools/lib-test-env.sh
          test_env_begin
          mkdir -p target/floats
          cc -std=c11 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 notes/yw07b-evidence/floats/oracle.c -o target/floats/oracle
          python3 -I notes/yw07b-evidence/floats/corpus.py target/floats/corpus.txt
          python3 -I notes/yw07b-evidence/floats/host.py target/floats/corpus.txt target/floats/oracle target/floats/host
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: float-oracle-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: target/floats/host/
float-hosts.yml.compare:
needs: oracle
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: float-oracle-*
          path: target/float-hosts
      - name: Reject broadened float-host exceptions
        run: python3 -I notes/yw07b-evidence/floats/host-compare-test.py target/float-hosts/controls
      - name: Refuse unruled host-divergent C conversions
        run: |
          python3 -I notes/yw07b-evidence/floats/corpus.py target/float-hosts/corpus.txt
          python3 -I notes/yw07b-evidence/floats/host-compare.py target/float-hosts/float-oracle-ubuntu-24.04 target/float-hosts/float-oracle-macos-14 target/float-hosts/comparison.json target/float-hosts/corpus.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: float-host-comparison
          path: target/float-hosts/comparison.json

toyvm.yml.collector:
